sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: This entry points to Dobharchú, also written Dorraghow, Dobharchu, or Otter King. Dobharchú is an Irish folkloric figure. He was the unsleeping king of the otters. He had black-and-white stripes. He was a supernatural being who hunted and killed humans. He was hard to kill. He was vulnerable only to silver bullets. Hunting him was dangerous. A successful hunter often died within a day. Some still took the risk. The king otter's hide was valuable. Even a small piece of the hide kept its holder from drowning. Merchants sold bits of ordinary otter fur into historical times. The fur went to sailors. Sailors had great need of protection from death by water. Several families claimed descent from otters. The McMurrows were the most notable.
objective: Records the Dobharchú (Dorraghow), the king otter whose hide protected from drowning and whose killing brought danger.
